newsitem.title: USA: PG&E plans stranded asset bond offer 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: PG&E plans stranded asset bond offer 1997-98.

text.p: San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric Co (PG&E) plans to offer up to $2.5 billion in "stranded cost" bonds between late 1997 and early 1998, a company spokeswoman said Friday.
The term "stranded costs" refers to assets, such as nuclear plants and power-purchase contracts, that would not be cost-competitive after the electricity industry undergoes deregulation.

Under legislation passed in California this year, the California Infrastructure Bank was authorized to issue up to $10 billion in revenue bonds to help the state's major investor-owned utilities pay off their stranded costs.
The securities will be backed by "competitive transition charges" paid by utility customers.
PG&E estimates its total stranded costs at $10 to 14 billion, but consumer advocates and others have questioned the figures.
The utility has retained Morgan Stanley and Co as lead underwriter and consultant for the securities, said spokeswoman Diane Sable.
